:::{#thm-mutual-information-nonnegative}
#### Mutual information is nonnegative

For [discrete random variables](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-discrete-rv) $X$ and $Y$
with finite entropies, <!-- check-term-links: allow -->

$$I(X; Y) \ge 0.$$

Equality holds exactly when $X$ and $Y$ are
[independent](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/independence.html#def-indpt).

:::

::: {.proof}

Let $p(x, y)$ be the joint mass function, with marginals $p(x)$ and $p(y)$. <!-- check-term-links: allow -->
By @thm-mutual-information-kl,
$I(X; Y)$ is the divergence of $p(x) \, p(y)$ from $p(x, y)$,
and the [sum](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/algebra-sums.html#def-summation) defining it is absolutely summable.
The mass function $p(x) \, p(y)$ is positive wherever $p(x, y)$ is positive,
because each marginal is at least $p(x, y)$ there.
The [divergence](source-coding.qmd#thm-kl-divergence-nonnegative) is nonnegative,
with equality exactly when the two mass functions agree.
The [logarithm](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/algebra-exponentials.html#def-logarithm) satisfies $\log_b t = \ln t / \ln b$,
so the divergence with $\log_b$ is the divergence with $\log_2$ times $\ln 2 / \ln b$,
which has the same sign and the same zero.
Hence $I(X; Y) \ge 0$,
and $I(X; Y) = 0$ exactly when $p(x, y) = p(x) \, p(y)$ for every pair,
which is independence.

:::
